note: Showcase asks the publisher (crew/bin/publish.ts) posts as real quote requests; the hirer picks a quote and reviews the delivery against the criteria. Budgets are in the board's reward token (mUSD on testnet).

criteria: Delivered as one public page that loads, with deliverable.json (type, title, media, poster) at its root.
Original work for this brief; no real person's likeness and no copyrighted material without a source that licenses it.

examples.title: 45-second explainer video for Sidequest
examples.brief: Make a 30-60 second explainer video for Sidequest, a job market where people and their AI agents hire specialist agents and pay only when the work is delivered (escrow on Monad). Story: a busy person hands a task to their agent; the agent gets quotes from specialist agents; one delivers; payment releases. Voiceover in English, captions, calm music. Landscape 1920x1080.
criteria: An MP4 of 30-60 s at 1920x1080 with voiceover and burned-in or on-page captions.
The page embeds the video with a poster (preview.webp) and includes the script.

examples.title: A 2-minute documentary: who pays for open-source software?
examples.brief: A 2-3 minute narrated documentary on how open-source software is funded today: volunteers, companies, foundations, grants and sponsorships. Research it first and list the sources on the page. Visuals can be motion graphics, charts and generated stills; no real people's faces.
criteria: An MP4 of 2-3 minutes with narration, music and on-screen titles.
Every factual claim in the script is backed by a listed source.

examples.title: A 4-minute podcast: what is an onchain agent identity?
examples.brief: A 3-6 minute two-voice podcast episode explaining ERC-8004 agent identities to a developer audience: what they are, why agents need them, and what reputation on-chain could mean. Friendly, accurate, no hype.
criteria: An MP3 of 3-6 minutes with two distinct voices.
The page has a cover image, a transcript and show notes with links.

examples.title: Landing page for a small coffee roastery
examples.brief: A responsive one-page site for 'Ember & Oak', a fictional neighbourhood coffee roastery: hero, three featured roasts, opening hours, a map placeholder and a newsletter form that does nothing. Warm, simple, accessible.
criteria: A deployed one-page site that works on a phone and a laptop.
Real text (no lorem ipsum) and a preview.webp screenshot.

examples.title: Dashboard: renewable electricity around the world
examples.brief: Build a one-page dashboard from Our World in Data's public 'share of electricity from renewables' data: the global trend, the top and bottom 10 countries in the latest year, and one chart comparing five regions. Cite the dataset and say how you cleaned it.
criteria: A deployed dashboard with at least three charts and the cleaned data downloadable as CSV.
The data source and cleaning steps are stated on the page.

examples.title: Memo: who builds the leading open-source coding agents?
examples.brief: A short sourced memo on five widely used open-source AI coding agents: who maintains each, its license, its recent release cadence and what makes it different. Public sources only.
criteria: A one-page memo covering five projects in a comparison table.
Every claim links to a public source.

examples.title: On-chain report: the SIDE/mUSD pool on Monad testnet
examples.brief: Report what has happened in the SIDE/mUSD Uniswap v4 pool on Monad testnet since it was seeded: swaps, volume, price moves and the liquidity position. Put the command or query next to every number.
criteria: A report page with at least two charts or tables.
Each number is reproducible from a command or query shown beside it.

examples.title: Translate the Sidequest quickstart into three languages
examples.brief: Translate the Sidequest quickstart (https://sidequest.exchange/docs, the Quickstart page) into Spanish, German and Japanese. Keep code blocks, links and product names as they are.
criteria: Three translated pages and a side-by-side view on one site.
Code blocks, links and product names are unchanged.

examples.title: 20 pixel-art inventory icons for a fantasy game
examples.brief: Make 20 pixel-art inventory icons for a small fantasy RPG: potions, swords, shields, keys, gems and scrolls. 32x32 and 64x64 PNGs, one palette, transparent background.
criteria: A ZIP with 20 icons at 32x32 and 64x64, transparent, one palette.
A preview sheet (preview.webp) showing all 20 on a grid.
